Class VirtualViewTCP

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsoft.mesos.server.network.tcp.VirtualViewTCP
All Implemented Interfaces:
ClientConnection, Listener, VirtualView, Closeable, AutoCloseable, Runnable
public class VirtualViewTCP extends Object implements VirtualView, ClientConnection, Runnable, Listener
TCP implementation of the server-side virtual view for one connected client.

In the project architecture, a virtual view is the network boundary that hides the transport protocol from controllers and models. This concrete class is used for TCP clients: it owns the accepted client Socket, reads raw JSON lines from it, sends JSON responses back to it, and exposes the same server-facing contracts used by the rest of the application.

Incoming traffic follows this path: the TCP stream is read line by line in run(), each raw line is delegated to ClientCommandHandler, and the resulting client payload is routed through MessageRouter together with the assigned session id. The virtual view does not execute pre-lobby, lobby, or game rules; it only attaches the network session to the command routing layer.

Outgoing traffic follows the opposite path: controllers and models notify this object through Listener.notifyUpdate(ServerPayload), passing a typed ServerPayload. The virtual view converts that payload into the correct ServerMessageType, wraps it in a ServerMessage, serializes it as JSON, and writes it to the TCP socket.

The class also participates in the connection lifecycle. It implements ClientConnection so the ping-pong routine can send pings and close the connection, and it implements VirtualView so the command handler can report client messages and pong replies back to the server-side session logic.

    • VirtualViewTCP

      public VirtualViewTCP(Socket clientSocket, ServerConnectionLifecycle serverConnectionLifecycle, MessageRouter router, PrintStream out)
      Creates a TCP virtual view for one accepted client socket.

      The constructor opens the UTF-8 writer used for outgoing messages, registers this virtual view as a new client connection, stores the assigned session id, and creates the command handler that will parse incoming TCP messages.

      Parameters:
      clientSocket - accepted socket connected to one TCP client
      serverConnectionLifecycle - manager used for session registration, pong recording, and disconnection
      router - router used to send parsed client payloads to the correct server phase
      out - stream used for diagnostic TCP messages
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if clientSocket, serverConnectionLifecycle, or out is null
      IllegalStateException - if the output writer cannot be opened on the client socket

  • Method Details

    • run

      public void run()
      Runs the TCP reading loop for this client.

      The method reads one line at a time from the socket using UTF-8. Each line is treated as one JSON client message and passed to ClientCommandHandler. If parsing or dispatching that message fails, the exception is converted into an error response and sent to the same client without stopping the loop immediately.

      When the stream ends, the socket fails, or the thread exits the loop, the virtual view closes itself and triggers the normal server disconnection flow.

      Specified by:
      run in interface Runnable

    • describeSession

      public String describeSession()
      Returns a human-readable name for this client session.

      The nickname is read from the session registry when authentication has already completed. Before authentication, the method returns a fixed label used in TCP diagnostic messages.

      Returns:
      authenticated nickname, or unauthenticated-client

    • handleClientMessage

      public void handleClientMessage(ClientMessage clientMessage)
      Routes a parsed client message into the server command layer.

      The message has already been validated and deserialized by ClientCommandHandler. This method attaches the current session id and forwards only the payload to MessageRouter, because routing is based on the session phase and on the payload command type.

      Specified by:
      handleClientMessage in interface VirtualView
      Parameters:
      clientMessage - typed client message produced from the TCP JSON input

    • notifyUpdate

      public void notifyUpdate(ServerPayload payload)
      Sends a server-side update to the TCP client.

      Models and controllers use the generic ServerPayload hierarchy, while the network protocol requires a ServerMessageType. This method performs that mapping for every server payload currently supported by the TCP protocol and writes the resulting message to the socket.

      Specified by:
      notifyUpdate in interface Listener
      Parameters:
      payload - typed payload produced by server-side model or controller logic

    • sendPing

      public void sendPing()
      Sends a keep-alive ping to the TCP client.

      This method is called through the ClientConnection interface by the ping-pong routine. The ping has no payload: the message type is enough for the client to answer with a pong.

      Specified by:
      sendPing in interface ClientConnection

    • pong

      public void pong(PongPayload payload)
      Records a keep-alive pong received from the TCP client.

      The pong payload is produced by the command handler after it recognizes a ClientMessageType.PONG message. A non-null payload means the client respected the common TCP message envelope, so the session timestamp can be refreshed through the server connection lifecycle.

      Specified by:
      pong in interface VirtualView
      Parameters:
      payload - pong payload parsed from the client message envelope

    • closeSession

      public void closeSession()
      Closes this client session without exposing checked I/O errors.

      This method is the virtual-view level close operation used by server code that only needs to end the session. The actual idempotent cleanup is performed by close().

      Specified by:
      closeSession in interface VirtualView

    • close

      public void close() throws IOException
      Closes the TCP virtual view and starts server-side session cleanup.

      The method is idempotent: only the first call disconnects the session from the server connection lifecycle and closes the socket. Later calls return immediately. This is important because the socket reader, timeout routine, and external server code may all try to close the same connection.

      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
      Specified by:
      close in interface Closeable
      Throws:
      IOException - if closing the underlying socket fails
